# data/tracks/ — tracking output (generated by `src/track.py`)

For each video `<name>`:

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `<name>.csv` | One row per frame (columns below) |
| `<name>_overlay.mp4` | Video with the detected contour (green) and bounding box (blue). **Watch this to confirm the tracking is correct.** |
| `<name>_frames.jpg` | Contact sheet of numbered frames, used to choose `RELEASE_FRAME` in `src/config.py` |

## CSV columns

| Column | Unit | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| `frame` | – | frame index |
| `t` | s | time = frame / fps |
| `cx, cy` | px (1280-wide frame) | centre of the minimum enclosing circle |
| `w, h` | px | bounding-box width / height |
| `area` | px² | contour area (affected by camera zoom, **not** used for fitting) |
| `aspect` | – | bounding-box `h / w` (depends on squeeze direction, not used) |
| `elong` | – | ellipse minor/major axis, the **signal used for fitting** (scale- and rotation-invariant, 1 = round) |
| `fill` | – | area / enclosing-circle area (1 = perfect disc) |
| `solidity` | – | area / convex-hull area (< 1 means dents or concavities) |

During the press, the hand occludes part of the ball, so the shape numbers in that phase are unreliable. Only frames after release are used for fitting and validation.
